current_draft.content_markdown:
Riyadh — At the LEAP 2026 technology conference, [HUMAIN](https://data-volt.com/media/breaking-news/humain-partners-datavolt-develop-100mw-of-a-360mw-ai-datacenter-in-neom/) and [DataVolt](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/saudi-ai-firms-humain-datavolt-partner-data-center-kingdoms-red-sea-coast-2026-08-31/) announced the commencement of construction on a new 100MW artificial intelligence data center located at Oxagon in NEOM. This development marks a significant step in the region's digital infrastructure expansion, aiming to support the increasing global demand for AI computing power. The facility represents the initial phase of what is planned to be a massive 1.5GW AI data center campus, underscoring the scale of ambition driving Saudi Arabia's technological investments.

The announcement brings together HUMAIN's full-stack AI capabilities and DataVolt's expertise in developing sustainable digital infrastructure. According to the companies, this collaboration is designed to provide high-density digital infrastructure specifically tailored for advanced AI workloads. The integration of renewable energy sources and innovative cooling technologies is a central component of the project's design, reflecting a growing industry emphasis on sustainable computing practices. The first 100MW of capacity is anticipated to become operational by 2028. This partnership represents a notable convergence of software-driven artificial intelligence expertise and physical infrastructure development, creating a unified approach to addressing the complex demands of modern computing environments.

The scale of the planned campus is particularly noteworthy within the context of global data center development. While many facilities measure their capacity in tens of megawatts, the ultimate goal of a 1.5GW campus places this project among the most ambitious infrastructure initiatives currently underway. The initial 100MW phase serves as a critical proof of concept for the broader vision, demonstrating the feasibility of deploying high-density compute resources in a region that is rapidly positioning itself as a central hub for technological innovation. By targeting a 2028 operational date for the first phase, the companies are signaling their intent to move aggressively in a market characterized by intense competition and rapidly evolving technical requirements.

## Strategic Location and Infrastructure

The decision to locate the facility at Oxagon, NEOM's advanced manufacturing and innovation city, leverages several strategic advantages. Oxagon offers pre-zoned industrial land, substantial energy resources, and critical subsea cable connectivity. These elements are essential for establishing a robust data center capable of handling the intense computational requirements of modern AI applications. The location not only provides the necessary physical space and power but also ensures the high-speed data transmission required for global connectivity.

The partnership involves key leadership figures, with Tareq Amin serving as the CEO of HUMAIN, Rajit Nanda as the CEO of DataVolt, and Aiman Al-Mudaifer as the Managing Director and CEO of NEOM. Their involvement highlights the strategic importance of the project within the broader context of Saudi Arabia's economic diversification and digital transformation goals. The development aligns with the nation's vision to establish itself as a leading hub for technology and innovation in the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region. The presence of these executives at the announcement underscores the institutional backing and high-level coordination required to execute a project of this magnitude.

Furthermore, the integration of the facility into the broader NEOM ecosystem presents unique opportunities for synergistic development. Oxagon is designed to be a center for advanced and clean industries, making it an appropriate setting for a data center that emphasizes sustainability and high performance. The availability of pre-zoned industrial land reduces administrative friction, allowing for accelerated construction timelines. Meanwhile, the subsea cable connectivity ensures that the facility can integrate directly into global data networks, a critical requirement for serving international clients and supporting distributed artificial intelligence workloads.

## Regional Impact and Future Phases

The construction of this AI data center is poised to have a substantial impact on the regional technology landscape. By providing localized, high-performance computing resources, the facility can support a wide range of industries, from telecommunications to logistics and supply chain management. This infrastructure is critical for the deployment of advanced AI models, which require significant processing power and low-latency access to data. The project also signals a strong commitment to integrating Industry 4.0 technologies and supporting the Saudi digital economy.

As the first phase of a planned 1.5GW campus, the initial 100MW facility is just the beginning. The phased approach allows for scalable growth, ensuring that the infrastructure can adapt to future technological advancements and increasing market demand. The facility is part of the 360MW first phase of DataVolt's planned 1.5GW AI data center campus. However, the success of this ambitious project will depend on the timely execution of construction phases and the effective integration of the promised renewable energy and cooling technologies. The industry will be watching closely as the 2028 operational target approaches.

The phased expansion strategy mitigates some of the risks associated with large-scale infrastructure projects. By initially focusing on a 100MW deployment within a broader 360MW first phase, the partners can refine their operational models, optimize cooling systems, and establish reliable supply chains before scaling up to the full 1.5GW capacity. This approach also provides flexibility to incorporate newer, more efficient technologies as they become available, ensuring that the later phases of the campus remain competitive in a rapidly advancing field. The long-term vision reflects a sustained commitment to building out the digital foundation necessary for an artificial intelligence-driven economy.

## Addressing the AI Compute Demand

The global surge in AI development has created an large-scale demand for specialized data center infrastructure. Traditional data centers are often ill-equipped to handle the power density and cooling requirements of AI hardware. The HUMAIN and DataVolt project aims to address this gap by designing a facility from the ground up to support high-density AI workloads. This focus on specialized infrastructure is a critical differentiator in a highly competitive market.

While the announcement at LEAP 2026 provides a clear vision for the project, several material questions remain. The specific details regarding the sourcing of renewable energy and the exact nature of the innovative cooling technologies have yet to be fully disclosed. As the project progresses, stakeholders will look for further clarity on these operational aspects. The successful realization of the 100MW facility by 2028 will be a key milestone in demonstrating the viability of the broader 1.5GW campus plan.

The project will significantly enhance the region's capabilities in handling complex artificial intelligence tasks, providing a robust foundation for future technological advancements and economic growth across various sectors. The integration of renewable energy and advanced cooling is particularly crucial, as the environmental impact of artificial intelligence computing is becoming a central concern for both regulators and clients. If the partnership can successfully deliver on its promises of sustainability and high performance, the Oxagon facility could serve as a model for future developments in the region and beyond.
